variants.headline: A bargain with {{partner}}, and gold in the terms
body: We have struck terms with {{partner}}. Our side gives {{weGive}} and receives {{weGet}}, and gold is part of the bargain.

variants.headline: A bargain abroad, with the name left blank
body: Word of a bargain abroad came to the counting house with the other party's name missing. We give {{weGive}}; we take {{weGet}}. There is gold in the terms.

variants.headline: The terms of the bargain
body: We give: {{weGive}}.
We receive: {{weGet}}.
Gold in the terms: counted.

variants.headline: Hear it! Terms are struck with {{partner}}
body: Mark it, good people, mark it: terms are struck with {{partner}}! We give {{weGive}}. We take {{weGet}}. Gold is moving, and when gold moves, the market stalls feel it first. Mark the prices this week, and mark them well!

variants.headline: The envoys earn their keep
body: Citizens, we have a bargain with {{partner}}: we give {{weGive}}, we take {{weGet}}, and gold is in the terms. Striking one is slow, unglamorous work, done by envoys who get blamed when it fails and forgotten when it holds. This one holds. Remember the office that made it so.

variants.headline: A trade route bound for us is plundered
body: A trade route bound for our territory has been plundered on the road, and the run is lost. Our cities will go without whatever the caravan was carrying, and the road will be quieter for a while.

variants.headline: {{plunderer}} robs the road to our gates
body: {{plunderer}} has plundered a trade route bound for our gates, and the run is lost. Their riders knew the road and the schedule, which is worth thinking about. A raider fed once on our roads will come back for the next meal.

variants.headline: Payday for the raiders
body: The raid on a route bound for us paid the raiders {{gold}} gold. At the unloading yard a porter rubbed his rate off his little slate. He wrote WILL CARRY ANYTHING and set it back against his stool.

variants.headline: Trade needs a guarded road
body: We learn that a trade route on its way to our gates has been plundered on the open road. The ledgers can say to the coin what the run was carrying. What no ledger says is who was meant to be watching the road, and this paper has asked.

variants.headline: The road from {{origin}} is robbed
body: They say the run out of {{origin}} never finished. Robbers had it on the road, and nothing came through. The far end loses its goods, our end loses its market, and the robbers eat well.

variants.headline: Our outgoing trade has stopped
body: Our last outgoing trade route has ended, and no trade of ours now sets out for a foreign market. The caravan is unharnessed, and the foreign coin that used to arrive with it has stopped.

variants.headline: The weights are put away
body: Here ends the account of our last outgoing trade route. In the merchant's yard, the keeper of the scales wrapped the weights in wool and laid them in their chest.

variants.headline: Small exporters have less room to wait
body: We had {{routes}} outgoing trade routes at the last count. With all of them gone, a merchant can't move a waiting shipment onto another run. The big houses can rent another shed and wait. Smaller shops may have to cut production before they run out of room for stock.

variants.headline: Notice to those who send trade out
body: Notice to shippers and warehousemen: our outgoing trade routes have ended, and we run none. Goods meant for foreign markets must wait for a new road or go into storage. The workshops keep making; the roads, for the present, carry nothing out.

variants.headline: Trade run complete between cities {{routeDistance}} tiles apart
body: The trade run linking {{ourCity}} and {{theirCity}} has finished. The cities lie {{routeDistance}} tiles apart on the survey map. A shopkeeper who followed the run is already asking whether the merchants plan to make it again.

variants.headline: The next order from {{theirCity}}
body: Merchants from {{ourCity}} have completed a long trade run to {{theirCity}}. If somebody makes a regular trip of it, a buyer there can ask for a particular cloth and expect it on a later run. A weaver here could start making cloth to order instead of packing a bolt and hoping it suits.

variants.headline: A long road ends at {{ourCity}}
body: Letters from the road relate that a caravan out of {{theirCity}} has completed the {{routeDistance}}-tile journey to {{ourCity}}. To walk so far to sell to us is a compliment of some weight, and our merchants, we trust, returned it. Fuller stalls will do the rest.

variants.headline: A trade run with {{partner}} enters the record
body: In this season the trade run between {{ourCity}} and {{theirCity}}, which lie {{routeDistance}} tiles apart, was completed. The annalist set down both names under the heading for {{partner}}, so that a reader of the account may know how far the trade reached.

variants.headline: A {{routeDistance}}-tile run, completed
body: The {{ourCity}} to {{theirCity}} route just finished the full {{routeDistance}}-tile run. That's a lot of map between two markets, and the cargo saw every tile of it.

variants.headline: Our trade route plundered on the road
body: A trade route out of our territory has been plundered on the road, short of its destination. The run is lost, and with it the goods and the gain our side was owed for the journey.

variants.headline: {{plunderer}} takes our trade on the road
body: Our caravan never made it. {{plunderer}} had it on the road, and the loss lands here at home, in the wages it was to earn and the stalls it was to supply. The men who sent it out are not the ones who are short tonight.

variants.headline: The account of a plundered route
body: Route lost: one, out of our territory.
Gold carried off: {{gold}}.
Balance of the day: against us.

variants.headline: Trade route to {{destination}} plundered
body: A trade route of ours bound for {{destination}} has been plundered. At the dispatch yard, one merchant is thinking of the people who were expecting a delivery. "I'd like to get word to them," she says. "At least they'd know to look somewhere else."

variants.headline: Send the spears with the trade
body: Citizens, another of our caravans has been taken on the road, and the answer from the capital is the same silence as the last time. Robbery is cheap because we have made it cheap. Put guards on the roads and watch the price of robbery rise. We want our trade defended, and we want the next raider to meet somebody.

variants.headline: Our trade goes abroad
body: Our outgoing trade routes now number {{routes}}, where at the last count there were none. The first caravans are out on the roads, and the goods they carry will come home again as coin.

variants.headline: Hear it! Our trade goes abroad
body: Hear it, people, hear it! The roads are open! {{routes}} trade routes of ours now go out to foreign markets, where before there were none! Our goods go out, our name goes with them, and the coin comes home! Mark it well!

variants.headline: What a new market can do for one kiln
body: The government's new trade network has {{routes}} routes abroad. A potter who used to fire a half-empty kiln for the home market can spend less on fuel per bowl if buyers in a second town help her sell a whole batch. A market abroad could make bowls cheaper here at home.

variants.headline: The road out stands open
body: Where the road goes out, the gold comes home.

variants.headline: We plunder a foreign trade route
body: Our forces have plundered a trade route out of foreign territory, and the run is at an end. The goods it carried are ours now, and the road it used will be quiet for a while.

variants.headline: {{gold}} gold taken from a foreign route
body: Our forces plundered a foreign trade route on the road and took {{gold}} gold from the run. The coin is in our treasury now. The loss sits in somebody else's books, and they know where to find us.

variants.headline: A route from {{origin}} to {{destination}} is plundered
body: Our forces have brought a trade route from {{origin}} to {{destination}} to an end on the road, and the goods are in our keeping. We do not doubt the taking was profitable. We note only that a nation of standing robs its neighbors' commerce on principle or not at all, and principle appears to have been absent here.

variants.headline: Foreign trade turns a profit
body: Foreign trade routes, it turns out, pay well. You just have to collect in person.

variants.headline: Have we no merchants left?
body: Sir, I have sold across borders all my working life, and my ledgers are full of names I would rather not rob. The route our soldiers took on the road was carrying, among other goods, the goodwill that lets the next caravan pass. We will want those roads again one day, and they will remember who was standing on them.
